# Unignoring an older non-self-ignored venv can add generated files to jj changes

Reviewed commit: 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db

## TLDR

Source-confirmed review record: A checkout that still holds the old tmux Python environment from Python 3.12 or earlier can expose generated files to automatic tracking when the root ignore is removed. This is conditional maintainer checkout pollution. The original claim that the whole roughly 350 MB environment is swept into the next change is retracted: inclusion is per file, subject to jj's maximum and all applicable ignore rules. Original consequence preserved and calibrated: small generated files can enter a working-copy change and create review/cleanup noise; no aggregate tracked size or accidental committed payload has been observed. Source route: 0503114305dccf054d575faca3e2e35d1b6010c1:scripts/build-pinned-tmux-ci.sh:29-31,44-61 places python_env at .ci-tmux-python, invokes plain python3 -m venv and installs ziglang on Linux x86_64/arm64, without pinning the Python version. e1817212f18c02109c9c469001af8cc6644a9324 replaces this persistent environment with a temporary one and adds rm -rf of old residue. d751ff16 deletes that script and removes the .ci-tmux-python/ root ignore while retaining .ci-tmux/. The pre-deletion script's lines 30-33 explicitly document old residue outside cargo clean. Current ordinary cleanup search: git grep at pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db over scripts, .agents, .github, docs and deflake found no ci-tmux-python or tmux-python reference; the sole ci-tmux match is .gitignore:33. Read-only jj --ignore-working-copy config list --include-defaults snapshot confirms all() and max-new-file-size 1MiB for this checkout. This is a per-file bound, not an aggregate-directory allowance. Python caveat checked through official contracts and source: Python 3.13 introduced venv's default .gitignore; CPython v3.13.0 Lib/venv/__init__.py:260-270 writes a star rule covering the entire environment, so an intact environment created by the old producer under 3.13+ remains ignored even without the root rule. CPython v3.12.0 create():54-79 has no SCM-ignore phase and create_configuration():169-201 writes pyvenv.cfg; normal venv metadata and activation scripts are small generated files outside the root ignore's remaining patterns. Exact jj oversized-file behavior is now source-checked for installed version 0.47.1: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jj-vcs/jj/v0.47.1/lib/src/local_working_copy.rs :1687-1727 checks ignore and automatic-tracking eligibility first, then sends FileTooLarge and returns Ok(None) for a new over-limit file; otherwise it processes that file normally. Thus a large zig executable is left untracked rather than making the whole snapshot fail solely for its size, and independently eligible small environment files can still enter the tree. The official configuration contract at https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/config/#maximum-size-for-new-files agrees on the default 1MiB per-new-file cap. This is source analysis, not observed snapshot behavior.
